questions: If there are multiple possible rectangles that could contain all black cells, is it sufficient that at least one such rectangle can be formed, or must the rectangle be uniquely determined?
Must the rectangle of black cells be axis-aligned with the grid (i.e., sides parallel to rows and columns), or are rotated rectangles allowed?
Are cells outside the chosen rectangle required to be white, or can they remain black if they were originally black but lie outside the rectangle?
When painting “?” cells, are we allowed to change already painted black (“#”) or white (“.”) cells, or must those remain unchanged?

If the initial configuration already contains black cells that are not contiguous (e.g., separated by white cells), is it still possible by painting “?” cells, or must the existing black cells themselves already form a rectangle?
In the case where the only black cells are isolated (e.g., a single black cell), is a 1×1 rectangle considered valid?
Should the output be exactly “Yes”/“No” with that capitalization and no extra whitespace or newline characters?
Are there any constraints on the total number of “?” cells (e.g., can they be zero), and does the answer change if there are no “?” cells at all?
answers: Related — existence of one such rectangle is what's defined; uniqueness isn't addressed.
The rectangle is axis-aligned — defined by row range [a,b] and column range [c,d], not rotated.
Related to the rectangle definition — cells outside [a,b]x[c,d] must be white, per the definition given.
Not addressed by the given clarification.
Not addressed by the given clarification.
Not addressed; a 1x1 region satisfies the same a=b, c=d definition.
Not addressed; assume standard exact Yes/No output.

inline_prompts:
You are given a grid of H rows and W columns.
Let (i,j) denote the cell at row i (1 \leq i \leq H) from the top and column j (1 \leq j \leq W) from the left.
The state of the grid is represented by H strings S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_H, each of length W, as follows:
- If the j-th character of S_i is #, cell (i,j) is painted black.
- If the j-th character of S_i is ., cell (i,j) is painted white.
- If the j-th character of S_i is ?, cell (i,j) is not yet painted.
Takahashi wants to paint each not-yet-painted cell white or black so that all the black cells form a rectangle.
Determine whether this is possible.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
H W
S_1
S_2
\vdots
S_H
Output
If it is possible to paint all the not-yet-painted cells so that the black cells form a rectangle, print Yes; otherwise, print No.
Constraints
- 1 \leq H, W \leq 1000
- H and W are integers.
- Each S_i is a string of length W consisting of #, ., ?.
- There is at least one cell that is already painted black.
